tests.stimulus: Assert reset_n=0 across three rising edges initially and between every directed scenario; drive valid/wr=0, release on a falling edge and wait 4100 rising edges. Observe all valid flags during reset and verify an unwritten fid with a nonzero packet serial after release. Include another reset with queued type3 beats before draining.
tests.expected: Inputs are binary and sampled on rising clk edges. reset_n is synchronous active low. A sampled reset clears all three output-valid flags and flushes pending packet decisions and queues; payload and metadata have no reset value while valid is low. The tables are automatically cleared to hash=0 and serial=0 by a scan of 4097 released-reset edges. During that scan table initialization overrides software writes. Wait 4100 released-reset edges before traffic or writes requiring a persistent entry. A later reset starts the same scan.
tests.checker: Drive on falling edges and sample one ns after rising edges. Use the same native-port input-history dvbench_model in an independent prediction instance; it cannot read actual outputs. Compare PP, ECDSA and HASH event queues with four-state field checks, mask only type2 final low16, and raise UVM_ERROR on mismatch, extra/missing beats or failure to drain. Require at least100 compared events globally; check reset valid flags separately.

tests.stimulus: After initialization, write fid values 0,17,4095 with zero and nonzero hash, serial 0,0x1234 and all ones, PPL 0/63; use consecutive writes and overwrite a previous serial. With ready both 0 and 1 send type1 SOP serials equal to and different from the stored value, observing the selected output. Include read/write collision at a SOP and use the pre-write entry.
tests.expected: ecdsa_lh_wr captures the 12-bit address, 256-bit hash, 64-bit serial and 6-bit PPL together. Outside initialization that update commits on the next rising edge; ecdsa_lh_ready never gates it or packet reads. Consecutive writes are accepted. Read/write collision uses the pre-write table contents. At non-type3 SOP the fid selects the stored hash; type1 also selects the serial. The packet serial is the low 64 bits of the SOP header. PPL is stored but has no observable effect at these output ports.

tests.stimulus: Send stable per-packet metadata with every field varied across packets, lengths 1,5,8,12,62 and valid gaps of 0,2,4 clocks, using nonoverlapping SOP/EOP and no queue overflow. Invalid cycles toggle headers and do not create expected beats.
tests.expected: Each valid input beat contains a 128-bit header, SOP/EOP and native metadata. There is no input ready. SOP establishes type3, with type3 taking precedence over type1; otherwise type1 or ordinary type2 is selected. That class persists across valid gaps until the accepted EOP. Metadata is carried per beat, and class/fid must be stable throughout one packet. Well-formed nonoverlapping packets of 1..62 beats are supported; do not exceed 64 buffered beats on either payload path or two pending non-type3 lookup results. Output payload/metadata/SOP/EOP are observed only with their valid flag; invalid-cycle values are unspecified.

tests.stimulus: Drive type3 and type1+type3 packets of length1,8,12,62, with isolated and interleaved ordinary packets; insert internal valid gaps. Give each beat a distinct input pattern and metadata. Drain for at least 180 cycles.
tests.expected: For type3 packets, every valid beat reaches PP unchanged, preserving SOP/EOP, all PP metadata fields and per-path order. No ECDSA data or generated-hash transaction belongs to a type3 packet. This also applies when type1 and type3 are both set. With no competing PP traffic the first beat appears four rising-edge intervals after its input sample; gaps in valid do not become output beats.

tests.stimulus: Initialize fid17 serial to0x1234, hash0. Send type1 serial0x7777 for mismatch and serial0x1234 for match, at lengths1,4,5,8,62. Repeat with nonzero hash in isolated long packets to expose optimistic early classification. Record expected ECDSA/PP queues from input only.
tests.expected: When the accepted hash classification permits normal handling, type1 with a different stored serial emits all original beats and all ECDSA metadata fields to ECDSA, preserving SOP/EOP. A matching serial routes to PP and removes the first four beats, with new SOP on input beat index 4 and EOP on the original last beat; indices start at zero. A shorter packet retains its last beat even when its index is below four, and that retained beat has SOP=0. Surviving PP metadata is preserved, including type1. A length-five matching packet produces one PP beat with both SOP/EOP set.

tests.stimulus: Drive ordinary type2 packets of length1,2,8,62 with distinct top16 and low112 values on every beat, including zero/full-scale/seed-random patterns, internal gaps and stable metadata. Drain at least180 cycles after EOP.
tests.expected: For an ordinary non-type3, non-type1 packet, PP output beat i before the tail concatenates input beat i bits 111:0 with input beat i+1 bits 127:112. SOP is on the first resulting beat. The last input beat also produces a tail: its upper 112 output bits equal that last input bits 111:0, EOP is set, and the final low sixteen bits are unspecified. For length N>=2 this produces N PP beats. A one-beat type2 packet produces an extra leading beat before the tail: its upper112 bits and SOP are the previously retained alignment history (initially unspecified, not reset); its low16 bits are that input header bits127:112, and EOP=0. Its subsequent tail has EOP=1 and the specified last-input upper112 relation. Metadata on aligned beats comes from the lookahead beat; the tail uses metadata held/available after the last payload read. Stable per-packet metadata removes that distinction.

tests.stimulus: With hash0 and a nonzero stored hash at fid17, compare isolated type1/type2 packets and a type3 packet immediately followed by a normal packet. Include short and long packets, back-to-back lookups within capacity, and gap placement before EOP to vary result availability.
tests.expected: The generator produces constant zero, rather than a cryptographic digest. Every valid non-type3 EOP produces a registered generated-hash result, and consuming a non-type3 SOP reports that generated value on lh_ecdsa_hash_data with lh_ecdsa_hash_valid. Hash and serial lookup results become available two and three rising-edge intervals after SOP respectively; buffered payload first becomes available three intervals after the input. The comparison is registered and treats either unavailable hash operand as a match. Consequently a nonzero stored hash alone does not guarantee discard: a normal class can latch before the generated value is available. Non-type3 reads are enabled one interval after their registered EOP result and continue through the last beat. When a head SOP sees a registered mismatch, discard handling suppresses all but its last beat and sets type3/discard in PP metadata. The pinned discard state clears on completion of a type1-to-PP conversion; reset also clears it. Do not replace this early-availability behavior by an ideal whole-packet hash comparison.

tests.stimulus: Alternate type3 and non-type3 packets, including type3 length20 followed by matching type1 length8 then type3 length8. Use per-packet tags to check PP ordering, concurrent ECDSA forwarding, ready0/1, and final empty queues after180 idle cycles.
tests.expected: PP arbitrates the bypass and normal paths at packet boundaries. After reset the normal path owns PP; an empty normal path releases it to bypass. Bypass keeps ownership through its EOP; when a normal PP class is waiting it hands over at bypass EOP or when bypass becomes empty. A normal PP EOP hands ownership to a nonempty bypass path. ECDSA type1 forwarding can proceed independently of PP ownership. Outputs have no reverse handshake and ecdsa_lh_ready is ignored. Preserve each output stream order without assuming input-order interleaving across paths or a common fixed non-type3 latency. Compare settled outputs after the rising edge; check exact defined fields, counts and bounded drain, and ignore only the explicitly unspecified type2 tail low sixteen bits.
